contents.html: Abstract. Mars, RC6, Rijndael, Serpent and Twofish were selected as finalists for the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). To evaluate the finalists’ suitability as random number generators, empirical statistical testing is commonly employed. Although it widely believed that these five algorithms are indeed random, randomness testing was conducted to show that there is empirical evidence supporting this belief. In this paper, NIST reports on the studies that were conducted on the finalists for the 192-bit key size and 256-bit key size. The results to date suggest that all five of the finalists appear to be random.
contents.html_ja: 概要。Mars、RC6、Rijndael、Serpent、Twofish が、高度暗号化標準（AES）の最終候補に選ばれました。最終候補が乱数生成器として適しているかどうかを評価するため、経験的な統計的検定が一般に用いられます。これら 5 つのアルゴリズムは実際にランダムであると広く信じられていますが、この信念を裏付ける経験的な証拠があることを示すために、ランダムネス検定を実施しました。本稿では、NIST が、192 ビット鍵長と 256 ビット鍵長について最終候補に対して実施した研究を報告します。現時点までの結果は、5 つの最終候補すべてがランダムであるように見えることを示唆しています。

contents.html: During the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) Round 1 analysis period, NIST conducted randomness tests focusing strictly on the 128-bit keysize case and reported on each of the fifteen candidate algorithms being considered for the standard [3]. contents.html: This paper describes how the output for each of the finalist algorithms was collected and then evaluated for randomness. It discusses what was learned utilizing the NIST statistical tests [2] and offers an interpretation of the empirical results. In Section 2, the Randomness Testing Experimental Setup is defined and described. In Sections 3 and 4, the Full Round Testing and Partial Round Testing efforts are discussed, respectively. Lastly, in Section 5, Summary and Conclusion, a final interpretation of the test results is drawn.

contents.html: Randomness testing activities can be divided into two parts. NIST analyzed the output for each of the five algorithms under full round and partial round considerations. All randomness testing was based on the application of the NIST Statistical Test Suite. This suite consists of 16 core statistical tests that, under different parameter inputs, can be viewed as 189 statistical tests. Table 1 lists each of the core statistical tests, followed by the number of P-values<sup>4</sup> reported by each core test and the test identifier. Each P-value corresponds to the application of an individual statistical test on a single binary sequence. For a brief description of each of these tests, see Appendix A. Full details documenting the derivation and description of the tests may be found in a forthcoming NIST publication [2].
contents.html_ja: ランダムネス検定の作業は 2 つの部分に分けられます。NIST は、5 つのアルゴリズムそれぞれの出力を、全ラウンドと部分ラウンドの考慮の下で分析しました。すべてのランダムネス検定は、NIST の統計的検定スイートの適用に基づいています。このスイートは 16 の中核となる統計的検定から成り、パラメータ入力を変えると 189 の統計的検定と見なすことができます。表 1 は、中核となる各統計的検定を示し、続けて、各中核検定が報告する P 値<sup>4</sup>の数と検定の識別子を示しています。各 P 値は、単一の 2 値系列に対する個々の統計的検定の適用に対応します。これらの検定それぞれの簡単な説明は、付録 A を参照してください。検定の導出と説明を記録した詳細は、近く刊行される NIST の刊行物 [2] に記載されています。

contents.html: Randomness testing was performed using the following strategy:
contents.html_ja: ランダムネス検定は、次の方針で実施しました。

contents.html: (a) Input parameters such as the sequence length, sample size, and significance level5 were fixed for each sample6. These parameters were set at \(2^{20}\) bits, 300 binary sequences, and 0.01, respectively. For each binary sequence and each statistical test, a P-value was reported.
contents.html_ja: (a) 系列長、標本サイズ、有意水準5などの入力パラメータは、各標本6について固定しました。これらのパラメータは、それぞれ \(2^{20}\) ビット、300 個の 2 値系列、0.01 に設定しました。各 2 値系列と各統計的検定について、P 値が報告されました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。2の20乗を数式に、脚注番号5・6を上付きに、斜体を原本どおりに。

contents.html: (b) For each P-value, a success/failure assessment was made based on whether or not it exceeded or fell below the pre-selected significance level.
contents.html_ja: (b) 各 P 値について、あらかじめ選んだ有意水準を上回ったか下回ったかに基づいて、成功・失敗の評価を行いました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合し一致。

contents.html: (c) For each statistical test and each sample, two evaluations were made. First, the proportion of binary sequences in a sample that passed the statistical test was calculated. The P-value for this proportion is equal to the probability of observing a value equal to or greater than the calculated proportion. Second, an additional P-value was calculated, based on a \(\chi^2\) test (with nine degrees of freedom) applied to the P-values in the entire sample to ensure uniformity.
contents.html_ja: (c) 各統計的検定と各標本について、2 つの評価を行いました。第 1 に、標本の中で統計的検定に合格した 2 値系列の割合を計算しました。この割合に対する P 値は、計算された割合以上の値が観測される確率に等しくなります。第 2 に、標本全体の P 値に自由度 9 の \(\chi^2\) 検定を適用して、一様性を確認するための追加の P 値を計算しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。"c 2" はカイ二乗の記号。画像で確認し数式に。

contents.html: (d) For both measures described in step (c), an assessment was made. A sample was considered to have passed a statistical test if it satisfied both the proportion and uniformity assessments. If either of the two P-values in step (c) fell below 0.0001, then the sample was flagged as suspect<sup>7</sup>. If this occurred, additional samples were evaluated. Otherwise, the sample was believed to have satisfied the criterion for being random (from the point of view of a specific statistical test).
contents.html_ja: (d) 手順 (c) で述べた 2 つの尺度の両方について、評価を行いました。標本は、割合と一様性の両方の評価を満たした場合に、統計的検定に合格したと見なしました。手順 (c) の 2 つの P 値のいずれかが 0.0001 を下回った場合、その標本は疑わしいもの<sup>7</sup>として印を付けました。そのような場合には、追加の標本を評価しました。そうでなければ、その標本は（特定の統計的検定の観点から）ランダムであるための基準を満たしたものと見なしました。

contents.html: During the AES Round 2 analysis period, NIST further investigated the randomness of the output for each of the finalists. The range of analyses was extended beyond the 128-bit keysize case conducted during the AES Round 1 analysis period. In this study, empirical statistical testing was performed on the 192-bit and 256-bit key sizes under full round considerations. In addition, partial round testing was conducted for the 128-bit keysize case.
contents.html_ja: AES の第 2 ラウンドの分析期間中、NIST は、最終候補それぞれの出力のランダムネスをさらに調査しました。分析の範囲は、AES の第 1 ラウンドの分析期間中に実施した 128 ビット鍵長のケースを超えて拡張されました。本研究では、全ラウンドでの検討の下で、192 ビットと 256 ビットの鍵長について経験的な統計的検定を実施しました。加えて、128 ビット鍵長のケースについて部分ラウンド検定を実施しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合し一致。

contents.html: In each of these cases, a total of 189 statistical tests were applied on the different data sets. These tests collectively span many well-known properties that any good cryptographic algorithm should satisfy. These properties include the absence of any detectable correlation between plaintext/ciphertext pairs and the absence of any detectable bias due to single bit changes to a plaintext block, a 192-bit key or a 256-bit key.
contents.html_ja: これらのそれぞれのケースで、合計 189 の統計的検定を、異なるデータセットに適用しました。これらの検定は全体として、優れた暗号アルゴリズムが満たすべき多くのよく知られた性質を網羅しています。これらの性質には、平文と暗号文のペアの間に検出可能な相関がないこと、および、平文ブロック、192 ビットの鍵、または 256 ビットの鍵の 1 ビットの変化に起因する検出可能な偏りがないことが含まれます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合し一致。

contents.html: In one instance there was a statistical anomaly. Serpent’s plaintext/ciphertext correlation (based on 256-bit keys) yielded 12 rejections out of a sample of 300 binary sequences, using the aperiodic template statistical test. Subsequent experiments were conducted, and no other anomalies were detected.
contents.html_ja: 1 つのケースで、統計的な異常がありました。Serpent の平文と暗号文の相関（256 ビット鍵に基づく）は、非周期テンプレートの統計的検定を用いたところ、300 個の 2 値系列の標本のうち 12 個が棄却されました。追加の実験を実施しましたが、ほかに異常は検出されませんでした。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合し一致。

contents.html: The results for the partial round testing, based on 128-bit key plaintext low density data, indicate that Mars achieves randomness at round 6, RC6 at round 4, Rijndael at round 3, Serpent at round 4, and Twofish at round 2.
contents.html_ja: 128 ビット鍵の平文低密度データに基づく部分ラウンド検定の結果は、Mars は第 6 ラウンド、RC6 は第 4 ラウンド、Rijndael は第 3 ラウンド、Serpent は第 4 ラウンド、Twofish は第 2 ラウンドでランダムネスを達成することを示しています。

contents.html: In spite of an isolated statistical anomaly in Serpent, it is fair to state that all of the algorithms appear to have no detectable deviations from randomness.
contents.html_ja: Serpent に孤立した統計的異常があったものの、すべてのアルゴリズムは、ランダムネスからの検出可能な逸脱がないように見えると述べるのが妥当です。

contents.html: Monobit Test: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in a sequence are approximately the same as would be expected for a truly random sequence.
contents.html_ja: Monobit Test: この検定の目的は、系列中の 1 と 0 の数が、真にランダムな系列で期待される数とほぼ同じかどうかを判定することです。

contents.html: Block Frequency Test: The purpose of the block frequency test is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in each of M non-overlapping blocks created from a sequence appear to have a random distribution.
contents.html_ja: Block Frequency Test: ブロック頻度検定の目的は、系列から作られた M 個の重ならないブロックのそれぞれにおける 1 と 0 の数が、ランダムな分布を示しているように見えるかどうかを判定することです。

contents.html: Cumulative Sums Forward (Reverse) Test: The purpose of the cumulative sums test is to determine whether the sum of the partial sequences occurring in the tested sequence is too large or too small.
contents.html_ja: Cumulative Sums Forward (Reverse) Test: 累積和検定の目的は、被検系列に現れる部分系列の和が大きすぎるか小さすぎるかを判定することです。

contents.html: Runs Test: The purpose of the runs test is to determine whether the number of runs of ones and zeros of various lengths is as expected for a random sequence. In particular, this test determines whether the oscillation between such substrings is too fast or too slow.
contents.html_ja: Runs Test: ラン検定の目的は、さまざまな長さの 1 と 0 のランの数が、ランダムな系列で期待されるとおりかどうかを判定することです。特にこの検定は、そのような部分文字列の間の振動が速すぎるか遅すぎるかを判定します。

contents.html: Long Runs of Ones Test: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the longest run of ones within the tested sequence is consistent with the longest run of ones that would be expected in a random sequence.
contents.html_ja: Long Runs of Ones Test: この検定の目的は、被検系列中の最長の 1 のランが、ランダムな系列で期待される最長の 1 のランと整合しているかどうかを判定することです。

contents.html: Rank Test: The purpose of this test is to check for linear dependence among fixed length substrings of the original sequence.
contents.html_ja: Rank Test: この検定の目的は、元の系列の固定長の部分列の間に線形従属性がないかを調べることです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。検定名の太字・変数の斜体を原本どおりに。

contents.html: Discrete Fourier Transform (Spectral) Test: The purpose of this test is to detect periodic features (i.e., repetitive patterns that are near each other) in the tested sequence that would indicate a deviation from the assumption of randomness.
contents.html_ja: Discrete Fourier Transform (Spectral) Test: この検定の目的は、ランダムネスの仮定からの逸脱を示す、被検系列中の周期的な特徴（すなわち、互いに近くにある反復パターン）を検出することです。

contents.html: To examine the sensitivity of individual algorithms to changes in the plaintext, 300 binary sequences were analyzed. The 300 sequences were parsed from a string constructed as follows: given 19,200 random 128-bit plaintext blocks, and a 192-bit (or 256-bit) key of all zeroes, 2,457,600 derived blocks were concatenated. Each derived block was based on the XOR of the “ciphertext formed using the fixed 192-bit (or 256-bit) key and the random plaintext,” and the “ciphertext formed using the fixed 192-bit (or 256-bit) key and the perturbed random plaintext with the ith bit changed, for \(1 \le i \le 128\).” A total of 128 sets of derived blocks were formed for each random plaintext. All derived blocks were concatenated, and a total of 2,457,600 derived blocks resulted. The 300 sequences of 1,048,576 bits (8,192 blocks) were parsed from the concatenated derived blocks.
contents.html_ja: 個々のアルゴリズムの平文の変化に対する感度を調べるため、300 個の 2 値系列を分析しました。300 個の系列は、次のように構成した文字列から切り出しました。19,200 個のランダムな 128 ビット平文ブロックと、すべてゼロの 192 ビット（または 256 ビット）鍵が与えられたとき、2,457,600 個の派生ブロックを連結しました。各派生ブロックは、「固定の 192 ビット（または 256 ビット）鍵とランダムな平文を用いて形成した暗号文」と、「固定の 192 ビット（または 256 ビット）鍵と、\(1 \le i \le 128\) について i番目のビットを変更した摂動を加えたランダムな平文を用いて形成した暗号文」の XOR に基づいています。各ランダム平文について、合計 128 組の派生ブロックを形成しました。すべての派生ブロックを連結した結果、合計 2,457,600 個の派生ブロックとなりました。1,048,576 ビット（8,192 ブロック）の 300 個の系列は、連結した派生ブロックから切り出しました。

contents.html: To examine the sensitivity of individual algorithms to changes in the 192-bit (or 256-bit key), 300 binary sequences were analyzed in each case. The 300 sequences were parsed from a string constructed as follows: given 19,200 random 192-bit (256-bit) keys, and a plaintext of all zeroes, 2,457,600 derived blocks were concatenated. Each derived block was based on the XOR of the “ciphertext formed using the fixed plaintext and one of the random 192-bit (or 256-bit) keys,” and the “ciphertext formed using the fixed plaintext and a perturbed form of the random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key with the ith bit changed, for \(1 \le i \le 128\).” Note that bits 129-192 (or 129-256) are unchanged. A total of 128 sets of derived blocks were formed for each random key. All derived blocks were concatenated, and a total of 2,457,600 derived blocks resulted. The 300 sequences of 1,048,576 bits (8,192 blocks) were parsed from the concatenated derived blocks.

contents.html: 3 Plaintext/Ciphertext Correlation
contents.html_ja: 3 平文と暗号文の相関
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。付録内の項見出しをレベル3に。

contents.html: In order to study the correlation of plaintext/ciphertext pairs, 300 sequences (1,048,576 bits per sequence) were examined for each algorithm. Given a random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key and 8,192 random plaintext blocks, a binary sequence was constructed concatenating 8,192 derived blocks (where a derived block is the result of applying the XOR operator on the plaintext block and its corresponding ciphertext block computed in the ECB mode). Using the 8,192 (previously selected) plaintext blocks, the procedure was repeated 300 times, i.e., once for each (additional) random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key.
contents.html_ja: 平文と暗号文のペアの相関を調べるため、各アルゴリズムについて 300 個の系列（1 系列あたり 1,048,576 ビット）を検査しました。ランダムな 192 ビット（または 256 ビット）鍵と 8,192 個のランダムな平文ブロックが与えられたとき、8,192 個の派生ブロック（派生ブロックとは、平文ブロックと、ECB モードで計算したそれに対応する暗号文ブロックに XOR 演算子を適用した結果）を連結して、2 値系列を構成しました。8,192 個の（先に選んだ）平文ブロックを使って、この手順を 300 回、すなわち（追加の）ランダムな 192 ビット（または 256 ビット）鍵ごとに 1 回ずつ繰り返しました。

contents.html: Given a random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key, a 128-bit initialization vector (IV) of all zeroes, and 8,192 128-bit plaintext blocks (PT) of all zeroes, a binary sequence of 1,048,576 bits was constructed using ciphertext computed in the CBC mode. original_blocks.html: Randomness Testing of the Advanced Encryption Standard Finalist Candidates
Randomness Testing of the Advanced Encryption Standard Finalist Candidates1

Abstract. Mars, RC6, Rijndael, Serpent and Twofish were selected as finalists for the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). To evaluate the finalists’ suitability as random number generators, empirical statistical testing is commonly employed. Although it widely believed that these five algorithms are indeed random, randomness testing was conducted to show that there is empirical evidence supporting this belief. In this paper, NIST reports on the studies that were conducted on the finalists for the 192-bit key size and 256-bit key size. The results to date suggest that all five of the finalists appear to be random.
1 Introduction

During the AES Round 2 analysis period, NIST further evaluated the suitability of the five finalists as random number generators, focusing on the 192-bit and 256-bit keysize (under full round2 considerations) and the 128-bit keysize (under partial round3 considerations). As time permits, additional randomness testing efforts will be conducted.

This paper describes how the output for each of the finalist algorithms was collected and then evaluated for randomness. It discusses what was learned utilizing the NIST statistical tests [2] and offers an interpretation of the empirical results. In Section 2, the Randomness Testing Experimental Setup is defined and described. In Sections 3 and 4, the Full Round Testing and Partial Round Testing efforts are discussed, respectively. Lastly, in Section 5, Summary and Conclusion, a final interpretation of the test results is drawn.
2 Randomness Testing Experimental Setup

Randomness testing activities can be divided into two parts. NIST analyzed the output for each of the five algorithms under full round and partial round considerations. All randomness testing was based on the application of the NIST Statistical Test Suite. This suite consists of 16 core statistical tests that, under different parameter inputs, can be viewed as 189 statistical tests. Table 1 lists each of the core statistical tests, followed by the number of P-values4 reported by each core test and the test identifier. Each P-value corresponds to the application of an individual statistical test on a single binary sequence. For a brief description of each of these tests, see Appendix A. Full details documenting the derivation and description of the tests may be found in a forthcoming NIST publication [2].

(a) Input parameters such as the sequence length, sample size, and significance level 5 were fixed for each sample6. These parameters were set at 220 bits, 300 binary sequences, and 0.01, respectively. For each binary sequence and each statistical test, a P-value was reported.

(c) For each statistical test and each sample, two evaluations were made. First, the proportion of binary sequences in a sample that passed the statistical test was calculated. The P-value for this proportion is equal to the probability of observing a value equal to or greater than the calculated proportion. Second, an additional P-value was calculated, based on a c 2 test (with nine degrees of freedom) applied to the P-values in the entire sample to ensure uniformity.

(d) For both measures described in step (c), an assessment was made. A sample was considered to have passed a statistical test if it satisfied both the proportion and uniformity assessments. If either of the two P-values in step (c) fell below 0.0001, then the sample was flagged as suspect7. If this occurred, additional samples were evaluated. Otherwise, the sample was believed to have satisfied the criterion for being random (from the point of view of a specific statistical test).

FRT activities were conducted over a period of several months on multiple SUN Ultra8 workstations. All data was generated and evaluated online. Only the data used as the plaintext and the 192-bit and 256-bit keys were stored offline. These values were based on data generated using the Blum-Blum-Shub (BBS) pseudorandom bit generator9. All 189 statistical tests were applied to each data set as described in Appendix B.

4.1 Data Description

There were a few issues to address in defining partial round versions of the algorithms. If input whitening was prescribed (MARS, RC6, Rijndael, Twofish), then it was left intact; however, output whitening (MARS, RC6, Twofish) was omitted. In fact, the outputs of the final rounds for the algorithms were not considered at all, because full round testing was previously conducted for low-density plaintexts under 128 bit keys during AES Round 1 analysis. Subkeys were applied in their original order, as were rounds, so that if a modified final round was prescribed (Rijndael, Serpent), then it was never used.

Thus, the round outputs of RC6 were evaluated from rounds 1 to 19; Rijndael, from rounds 1 to 9; and Serpent, from rounds 1 to 31. For technical reasons, Twofish rounds were evaluated in pairs12, namely, the even numbered rounds from 2 to 14. MARS has a heterogeneous structure, so three different partial round versions were defined. First, the 8 preliminary, unkeyed, “forward mixing” rounds were left intact, and the outputs of each of the 16 keyed, “core” rounds were evaluated. Second, the forward mixing was disabled, and the outputs of the 16 core rounds were evaluated. Third, the outputs of the 8 forward mixing rounds were evaluated.

Appendix A Description of the Statistical Tests20
Monobit Test: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in a sequence are approximately the same as would be expected for a truly random sequence.

Block Frequency Test: The purpose of the block frequency test is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in each of M non-overlapping blocks created from a sequence appear to have a random distribution.
Cumulative Sums Forward (Reverse) Test: The purpose of the cumulative sums test is to determine whether the sum of the partial sequences occurring in the tested sequence is too large or too small.

Runs Test: The purpose of the runs test is to determine whether the number of runs of ones and zeros of various lengths is as expected for a random sequence. In particular, this test determines whether the oscillation between such substrings is too fast or too slow.

Long Runs of Ones Test: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the longest run of ones within the tested sequence is consistent with the longest run of ones that would be expected in a random sequence.
Rank Test: The purpose of this test is to check for linear dependence among fixed length substrings of the original sequence.

Discrete Fourier Transform (Spectral) Test: The purpose of this test is to detect periodic features (i.e., repetitive patterns that are near each other) in the tested sequence that would indicate a deviation from the assumption of randomness.
Aperiodic Templates Test: The purpose of this test is to reject sequences that exhibit too many occurrences of a given non-periodic (aperiodic) pattern.
Periodic Template Test: The purpose of this test is to reject sequences that show deviations from the expected number of runs of ones of a given length.

Universal Statistical Test: The purpose of the test is to detect whether or not the sequence can be significantly compressed without loss of information. A compressible sequence is considered to be non random.

Approximate Entropy Test: The purpose of the test is to compare the frequency of overlapping blocks of two consecutive/adjacent lengths (m and m+1) against the expected result for a normally distributed sequence.
Random Excursion Test: The purpose of this test is to determine if the number of visits to a state within a random walk exceeds what one would expect for a random sequence.
Random Excursion Variant Test: The purpose of this test is to detect deviations from the distribution of the number of visits of a random walk to a certain state.
Serial Test: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the number of occurrences of m-bit overlapping patterns is approximately the same as would be expected for a random sequence.
Lempel-Ziv Complexity Test: The purpose of the test is to determine how far the tested sequence can be compressed. The sequence is considered to be non-random if it can be significantly compressed
Linear Complexity Test: The purpose of this test is to determine whether or not the sequence is complex enough to be considered random.
Appendix B Description of the Data Types
1 Plaintext Avalanche

To examine the sensitivity of individual algorithms to changes in the plaintext, 300 binary sequences were analyzed. The 300 sequences were parsed from a string constructed as follows: given 19,200 random 128 bit plaintext blocks, and a 192-bit (or 256-bit) key of all zeroes, 2,457,600 derived blocks were concatenated. Each derived block was based on the XOR of the “ciphertext formed using the fixed 192-bit (or 256-bit) key and the random plaintext,” and the “ciphertext formed using the fixed 192-bit (or 256-bit) key and the perturbed random plaintext with the ith bit changed, for 1 £ i £ 128.” A total of 128 sets of derived blocks were formed for each random plaintext. All derived blocks were concatenated, and a total of 2,457,600 derived blocks resulted. The 300 sequences of 1,048,576 bits (8,192 blocks) were parsed from the concatenated derived blocks.
2 192-bit (or 256-bit) Key Avalanche

To examine the sensitivity of individual algorithms to changes in the 192-bit (or 256-bit key), 300 binary sequences were analyzed in each case. The 300 sequences were parsed from a string constructed as follows: given 19,200 random 192-bit (256-bit) keys, and a plaintext of all zeroes, 2,457,600 derived blocks were concatenated. Each derived block was based on the XOR of the “ciphertext formed using the fixed plaintext and one of the random 192-bit (or 256-bit) keys,” and the “ciphertext formed using the fixed plaintext and a perturbed form of the random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key with the ith bit changed, for 1 £ i £ 128.” Note that bits 129-192 (or 129-256) are unchanged. A total of 128 sets of derived blocks were formed for each random key. All derived blocks were concatenated, and a total of 2,457,600 derived blocks resulted. The 300 sequences of 1,048,576 bits (8,192 blocks) were parsed from the concatenated derived blocks.
3 Plaintext/Ciphertext Correlation

In order to study the correlation of plaintext/ciphertext pairs, 300 sequences (1,048,576 bits per sequence) were examined for each algorithm. Given a random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key and 8,192 random plaintext blocks, a binary sequence was constructed concatenating 8,192 derived blocks (where a derived block is the result of applying the XOR operator on the plaintext block and its corresponding ciphertext block computed in the ECB mode). Using the 8,192 (previously selected) plaintext blocks, the procedure was repeated 300 times, i.e., once for each (additional) random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key.
4 Cipher Block Chaining Mode

Given a random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key, a 128-bit initialization vector (IV) of all zeroes, and 8,192 128-bit plaintext blocks (PT) of all zeroes, a binary sequence of 1,048,576 bits was constructed using ciphertext computed in the CBC mode. That is, a binary sequence consisted of 8,192 concatenated 128-bit ciphertext blocks. The first ciphertext block (CT ) is defined by CT = E (IV ¯ PT ). Subsequent ciphertext blocks
were defined by CT = E (CT ¯ PT ) for 1 £ i £ 8,191. In all, 300 binary sequences were constructed,
i+1 k i i each with a different random 192-bit (or 256-bit) key.
5 Low Density Plaintext

Data sets were created based on low-density plaintext blocks. Each data set consisted of 300 sequences. Each sequence consisted of 8,257 ciphertext blocks, computed in the ECB mode, using a distinct random key per sequence. For low-density plaintext, two data sets were created, one using a random 192-bit key, and the other using a random 256-bit key. The first ciphertext block was calculated using an all zero plaintext block. Ciphertext blocks 2 - 129 were calculated using plaintext blocks consisting of a single one and 127 zeros, the one appearing in each of the 128 bit positions of the plaintext block. Ciphertext blocks 130 - 8,257 were calculated using plaintext blocks consisting of two ones and 126 zeros, the ones appearing in each combination of two bit positions of the plaintext block.

Each data set was encrypted under a distinct, randomly chosen key. For each algorithm, the round outputs were evaluated against all of the applicable tests. During the AES Round 2 analysis period, NIST further investigated the randomness of the output for each of the finalists. The range of analyses was extended beyond the 128-bit keysize case conducted during the AES Round 1 analysis period. In this study, empirical statistical testing was performed on the 192-bit and 256-bit key sizes under full round considerations. In addition, partial round testing was conducted for the 128-bit keysize case.

In each of these cases, a total of 189 statistical tests were applied on the different data sets. These tests collectively span many well-known properties that any good cryptographic algorithm should satisfy. These properties include the absence of any detectable correlation between plaintext/ciphertext pairs and the absence of any detectable bias due to single bit changes to a plaintext block, a 192-bit key or a 256-bit key.

In one instance there was a statistical anomaly. Serpent’s plaintext/ciphertext correlation (based on 256-bit keys) yielded 12 rejections out of a sample of 300 binary sequences, using the aperiodic template statistical test. Subsequent experiments were conducted, and no other anomalies were detected.

The results for the partial round testing, based on 128-bit key plaintext low density data, indicate that Mars achieves randomness at round 6, RC6 at round 4, Rijndael at round 3, Serpent at round 4, and Twofish at round 2.
In spite of an isolated statistical anomaly in Serpent, it is fair to state that all of the algorithms appear to have no detectable deviations from randomness.
